players.product: Ethernet switch / PHY and controller ICs

quarterly_data.signal: Deputy spokesperson Ivy Chen: Q2 2026 revenue reached TWD 37.6 billion, up 3.1% quarter-over-quarter and 17.7% year-over-year, supported by stable end-market demand and supply-chain-driven price increases, particularly in DRAM. Some customers maintained a solid order placement strategy on concern over supply constraints and further ASP increases in the second half. Q2 operating expenses TWD 13.9 billion (37.1% of revenue); operating profit TWD 3.73 billion (9.9% of revenue); net profit TWD 3.81 billion (10.1% of revenue); EPS TWD 7.42 vs TWD 8.44 in Q1 2026 and TWD 7.62 in Q2 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue TWD 37.6 billion, +3.1% QoQ, +17.7% YoY; operating margin 9.9%; EPS TWD 7.42

quarterly_data.signal: Ivy Chen: Q2 gross margin was 47.0%, down 2.7 percentage points from the previous quarter and 3.2 percentage points year-over-year, mainly driven by higher ASP reflecting OSAT capacity constraints from AI-related demand, higher DRAM memory prices and a higher mix of ICs with embedded memory. Management is optimising supply-side arrangements, improving product design and cost structure and reflecting cost increases where appropriate, and says these actions will support a gradual recovery in gross margin; longer term it sees room for further improvement from product mix and value-added products. OpEx ratio was 39.1% (Q3 2025), 39.2% (Q4 2025), 37.8% (Q1 2026) and 37.1% (Q2 2026); management expects it to remain stable at current levels in the short term, while absolute OpEx may remain relatively elevated with advanced-node designs.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 47.0% (down 2.7 points QoQ, 3.2 points YoY); OpEx ratio 37.1%

quarterly_data.signal: Management: the semiconductor value chain is experiencing a major structural supply shift driven primarily by the AI data center boom, creating critical shortages in advanced packaging, specialized materials and memory allocation. Q2 inventory turnover days were 107 (105 in Q1); a meaningful portion of inventory remains in work in process mainly due to the constraint in available OSAT capacity, as industry-wide capacity continues to be prioritized for AI server demand. Realtek has qualified multiple vendors to diversify supply and applies 'design for availability' principles to reduce exposure to constrained materials; it views around 100 days of inventory as normal and healthy, and says IC inventory at distributors and direct customers remains healthy.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory turnover 107 days (Q1: 105 days); around 100 days viewed as normal

quarterly_data.signal: Management: Realtek began working with customers on pricing in early June; new prices, where applicable, take effect in the third quarter to address rising memory prices, OSAT constraints and related cost increases, and potential further mature-node foundry wafer price increases in the second half. Very few, if any, products are likely to remain unaffected; product lines and magnitude were not disclosed (handled case by case). The memory price hike together with OSAT supply constraints has reached a level Realtek can no longer fully absorb on its own.
quarterly_data.figure: new prices effective Q3 2026; magnitude not disclosed

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 outlook (Ivy Chen): third-quarter demand expected to remain resilient though visibility varies by segment. PC demand likely to remain under pressure from higher DRAM, NAND and CPU costs after early order pull-ins, and management says Realtek's PC-related shipments are unlikely to grow sequentially in the second half; networking demand fundamentally stable (broadband upgrades, enterprise switch refresh, mix shift to Wi-Fi 7, mesh and tri-band routers); consumer mixed (TV softened after the 2026 FIFA World Cup, home appliances steady, game consoles may weaken); automotive steady to stronger in the second half. Realtek expects year-over-year growth this year in every segment it serves. Q2 sales mix was approximately 33% PC / 67% non-PC, vs 36% / 64% in the fourth quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: year-over-year growth expected in every segment this year; Q2 mix PC 33% / non-PC 67%

quarterly_data.signal: Management: Realtek showcased its 100G optical PHY at COMPUTEX Taipei 2026; the product is targeted to be ready for mass production as early as the first quarter of 2027. Initial focus is the 100G transceiver and active optical cable markets, whose TAM management assesses at around several hundred million US dollars per year. No sales-contribution guidance; the ramp depends on customer qualification and market adoption, and entry will be disciplined and gradual.
quarterly_data.figure: mass production as early as Q1 2027; TAM around several hundred million US dollars per year

quarterly_data.signal: Management: Realtek switch shipments remain weighted toward unmanaged products, but managed-switch shipment market share is estimated to have increased by roughly 2 to 3 percentage points from the previous reporting period. Realtek is pursuing project bids with leading managed-switch customers, including layer-three programs; given a typical 10 to 12 months development cycle, new design wins are more likely to contribute meaningful volume revenue in 2027 and 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: managed-switch share up roughly 2 to 3 percentage points; new design wins to contribute in 2027 and 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Management on servers: entry points are areas where Realtek already has IP - 10G Ethernet, I3C hubs, USB hubs, PON and Ethernet switch for the server control plane - with plans to expand to smart NICs, optical PHYs, high-speed data switches and more, using advanced process nodes and higher-grade quality standards. It is leveraging existing relationships and design wins with CPU, NPU and GPU solution providers and leading OEMs / ODMs, and approaching white-box-server ODMs. Realtek SSD controllers have been adopted by a leading GPU AI platform through its SSD module maker customers (management declined to comment on NVIDIA-related platforms).

Management on automotive Ethernet: first-half demand for Realtek automotive Ethernet is expected to continue into the second half; the main challenge is the supply side, given long qualification cycles for new automotive suppliers. Realtek cites its integrated Ethernet switch as the industry's first and only of its kind to achieve ASIL D functional safety, and its industry-first XL7 automotive Ethernet switch supporting up to four 10 gigabit-per-second links (company claims). Management sees no shortage of new design-win opportunities with tier 1s and OEMs across regions including China and Japan; it does not comment on market share.
quarterly_data.figure: XL7 switch: up to four 10 gigabit-per-second links; ASIL D

quarterly_data.signal: Management on Wi-Fi: Wi-Fi 7 notebook penetration is estimated to reach approximately 30% this year; broadband upgrades are constrained by higher DDR capacity requirements and system costs, and FTTR rollouts remain based on Wi-Fi 6. Wi-Fi 8 is expected to become a key technology focus from next year (plugfests underway), with commercial adoption first in PCs and routers, the earliest TV models around the first quarter of 2028, and tier 1 operators in Europe and North America expected to begin deploying Wi-Fi 8 routers in 2028. Management says Realtek's Wi-Fi development is on track and competitive. On broadband, 10G PON / XGS-PON is the baseline and tier 1 operators have begun testing 25G PON.
quarterly_data.figure: Wi-Fi 7 notebook penetration approximately 30% this year; Wi-Fi 8 routers in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Management: Realtek's TV SoC business grew above the corporate average in the first half, partly reflecting higher memory costs. In robotics, leading humanoid robot brands are adopting Realtek solutions in reference designs (Ethernet switches, USB hubs, Wi-Fi and other connectivity); management says the market remains in validation and may not reach broad adoption until later in the decade, and humanoids could offer greater silicon content per unit than automotive.
